chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The fasting one may submerge his body in the water, but he should not immerse his head.
ai.seo_question: Can a fasting person submerge their head in water according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the distinction between *istinqi'* (cooling or partial immersion) and *irtimas* (full head immersion), a key nuance in Shia fiqh regarding whether the fast is broken by water reaching the throat. This hadith reflects the scholarly consensus that mere contact or cooling does not invalidate the fast, whereas deliberate full immersion of the head is discouraged or considered breaking the fast depending on the school of thought, emphasizing precision in ritual practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Fasting-one can stay still in the water, and (but) he cannot immerse his head into the water’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man fasting can stay in water but cannot immerse his head in it.’”
